result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.has_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if an edge exists between two nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7399-L7490){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.has_edge( source, target, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Has edge](/assets/graphs/has-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared graph, directed. Left: querying A to B finds the accent edge from A to B, so has_edge returns True. Right: querying B to A, the reverse direction, finds only a dashed outline where that edge would be, so has_edge returns False." width="100%"} Answers the question "are these two nodes directly connected?" without needing to know any edge IDs. For undirected graphs, the order of `source=` and `target=` doesn't matter. For directed graphs, only an edge running from `source=` to `target=` counts; an edge in the reverse direction is ignored. Passing the same node as both endpoints checks for a self-loop. When several parallel edges join the pair, the result is still just `True`; use `find_edge_ids()` to retrieve all of them. Common uses include: - avoiding duplicate edges by checking before calling `add_edge()` - testing adjacency inside custom algorithms (e.g. "are two of my neighbors linked?") - checking for reciprocity in a directed graph by testing both directions The lookup scans the full edge list and ignores the current selection. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The first endpoint, as a node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). In a directed graph this is the node the edge must start from. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The second endpoint, as a node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). In a directed graph this is the node the edge must point to. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if at least one matching edge exists between the nodes, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` or `target=` is a label that doesn't belong to any node. (An integer ID that doesn't exist does not raise; it simply has no edges, so the result is `False`.) [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` or `target=` is neither an `int` nor a `str`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a directed graph, only the edge's actual direction is found: ::: {#eddae886 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B"), graph.has_edge(source="B", target="A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: In an undirected graph, the same edge is found regardless of which node is passed as `source`: ::: {#b076d1db .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B"), graph.has_edge(source="B", target="A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, True) ``` ::: ::: Checking before adding is an easy way to keep a graph free of parallel edges. The pair `("A", "B")` is already connected, so only the new `B--C` edge is added and the graph ends up with two edges: ::: {#58ad0de5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_node(label="C") for s, t in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "B")]: if not graph.has_edge(source=s, target=t): graph.add_edge(source=s, target=t) graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
